# Task
 Build the AutoSeguro WhatsApp insurance-sales agent for the KHAL FDE take-home challenge (deadline 2026-08-31; the PR must be ready by the evening of 2026-08-30) in this fresh repo.

 Read first:
 - $HOME/Downloads/<private-candidate-dossier> - sections 4 (challenge definition, plans/rules, API instability) and 8 (strategy, failure policy, handoff, observability, test cases). Personal file: context only, never copy it or its contents into the repo, and keep all PII out of commits.
 - $HOME/Projects/namastex-fde-challenge - the official challenge fork: quote-service (FastAPI; GET /health, GET /planos, POST /quote unstable: 20% 5xx, 10% slow by 8s), synthetic WhatsApp dataset, README. Run it locally with instability ON while developing. Read-only reference: never push there, never copy its git history.

 Shape (thin vertical slice, single app):
 - TypeScript + Node, CLI conversational channel that replays a WhatsApp-style chat. No web UI, no monorepo, no platform layers.
 - Deterministic core owns everything that matters: conversation state, required-field collection (plano, idade, ano do veiculo, CEP, data de inicio), validation before the API, quote-client resilience, handoff rules, audit trail. The LLM does language understanding and natural replies only; it never decides prices or handoff.
 - Failure policy per dossier section 8: timeout under 8s; at most 2-3 attempts with backoff and jitter; retry only on timeout/500/502/503; never on 400/422; never present an estimated or stale price as current; honest lead messaging; handoff carries reason + collected data + correlation id; statuses persisted for audit.
 - Traceability per event: conversation_id, message_id, timestamp, stage, collected fields + origin, quote_request_id, attempt, latency, HTTP status, outcome (resolved | awaiting_data | refused | handoff), handoff reason. No raw PII in logs (mask CPF, phone, email).
 - LLM provider: OpenAI-compatible client driven by env (LLM_BASE_URL, LLM_API_KEY, LLM_MODEL) so any provider works. If no usable key exists in the environment when you must record the real demo conversation, append `blocked: need LLM API key for demo conversation` and stop - firstmate will supply one.

 Definition of done (all of it in the PR):
 1. Happy path end to end: a real conversation obtains a real quote from the API (never an invented price; only the API prices and accepts).
 2. Failure behavior demonstrated and reproducible: timeout then success; 5xx until handoff; 422 without retry; duplicate message does not double-quote; resumed conversation keeps state; refusal cases (age above 75, vehicle older than 20 years) handled per the API's rules with handoff where commercial guidance is needed.
 3. README in pt-BR: run instructions (including the quote API), architecture, and engineering decisions and trade-offs - the failure policy front and center, understandable by another engineer.
 4. One complete logged conversation with a real quote under examples/ or docs/.
 5. Tests for the essential cases from dossier section 8: happy quote, high-risk CEP, age above 75, vehicle older than 20 years, mid-month start, timeout-then-success, 5xx until handoff, invalid payload without retry, duplicate message, conversation resume, logs free of CPF/phone/email in clear.
 6. ai-logs/ folder with a short README stating the AI conversation logs will be added at submission - the content is supplied by the captain, fabricate nothing.
 7. oxlint (complexity rules) + tsc wired in the repo, both clean. No code comments anywhere - constraints are encoded in types, assertions, and validation, never commented. No GitHub Actions, no release-please.
 8. README explains how an evaluator runs the quote API (point to the official challenge repo; vendor the service with attribution only if that is the simpler runnable path, and record the decision).

 Quote the API as the single price authority; your code validates inputs, it does not recompute quotes.

## Resumo

- entrega uma CLI TypeScript para conversa e replay no formato WhatsApp
- inicia `POST /quote` em background e responde imediatamente com estado `pending`
- mantém status e perguntas disponíveis durante timeout e retry
- persiste lifecycle `pending → retrying → delivered|failed`, tentativas e outbox
- invalida cotações antigas após correção e ignora respostas tardias
- faz handoff humano prevalecer sobre jobs em andamento
- usa Ollama Cloud apenas para compreensão e linguagem; decisões ficam no núcleo determinístico
- usa a API oficial como única autoridade de preço e aceitação

## Política de falha

- timeout de 3 segundos
- até 3 tentativas com backoff exponencial e jitter
- retry apenas em timeout, 500, 502 e 503
- 400 e 422 sem retry
- falha persistente ou recusa gera handoff com dados, tentativas e `quote_request_id`
- nenhum preço estimado, antecipado ou reaproveitado

## Evidência medida

`npm run evaluate -- --conversations 100` executou a API oficial com instabilidade 20%/10%, atraso de 8 s, seed 42 e concorrência 10:

- 100 conversas e 148 chamadas POST
- 95 cotações entregues e 5 handoffs esgotados
- 31 respostas 5xx e 22 timeouts
- acknowledgement p50 1 ms, p95 8 ms, máximo 12 ms
- 100/100 respostas de status durante `pending`
- 0 jobs duplicados
- 0 preços antes de confirmação
- 0 handoffs sem contexto
- 0 transições inválidas
- 0 vazamentos de PII nos artefatos
- 20/20 extrações corretas com Ollama Cloud DeepSeek V4 Flash

Artefatos:

- `examples/evaluation/reliability-100.json`
- `examples/evaluation/reliability-100.md`
- `examples/conversation-real.md`
- `examples/conversation-real.audit.jsonl`

```text
npm run check
22 testes aprovados
TypeScript limpo
oxlint limpo
```

Os testes forçam timeout→sucesso, 5xx→sucesso, falha mista, esgotamento, 422, 400, duplicata/status durante pending, correção durante pending, handoff antes de resultado tardio, outbox durável e retomada de processo.
